label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Hi Mikaela, yep we started on 21 September, after mating had started. Happy to give you the warts and all version, you were such a help to us when Dave did his shoulder.

We’re milking 290, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We skip Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday arvo milkings, so four once-a-day days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day, sadly no sleep-ins in the deal!

Production-wise, we’re down about 6% on milksolids for the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had said to expect 8–10%, so it’s been less of a hit than we’d braced for. That’s only a comparison with last year though, not proof that the milking change accounts for all of it. And we haven’t got through a whole season yet, so I can’t tell you what March looks like.

Cells did jump. We were around 110,000 and went up to about 180,000 for the first three weeks. Back around 135,000 now. So they didn’t go completely mental, but I wouldn’t tell you they stayed put either.

The worst bit was a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped arvo. We didn’t pick it up till the next morning and she lost a quarter. That’s the bit I wouldn’t gloss over. You really do have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days. Not going into the shed doesn’t mean you can just forget about them till morning, or it bites you.

The cows themselves came round quicker than I expected. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine. Lameness is way down too. We’ve got four on the lame list now against eleven this time last year. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so fewer trips must be a relief for them.

For us, the biggest difference has been having some life left outside milking. That first skipped Sunday arvo, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. We’d still milked that morning, but it felt like our first Sunday off in spring in twenty-odd years. Kieran, our 2IC, reckons it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That says quite a lot.

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. For us the hours alone are worth the 6%. With Tom’s knees as bad as you say, I reckon those arvos off could make a real difference, and I can understand why you’re looking at it with your young fella too. But I don’t want to sell you on it and have you cursing me in March! There’s a production cost, and the cow checks still need doing.

Come and find me at the field day on the 19th. I’ll bring our shed rosters and numbers so you can have a proper look at how we’re doing it. Or ring me whenever you want, much easier than texting with these useless thumbs.
